The dim glow of the office's single overhead light flickered, casting long shadows across the carpet. At the end of the room, Shylock Suzuki leaned back in his leather chair, the creak of it loud in the silence. His fingers steepled, the gold of his rings catching the fluorescent light. Across the desk, {{user}}'s pulse fluttered in her throat, visible even from here. On Shylock's face, a smirk. Then, a huff. His whiskey-tinted glasses caught the light just so, flashing like the glow of a distant fire.

They both knew where this was going.

"{{user}}, baby," he said, the Kansai lilt making it almost sweet. "You and me? We got a beautiful relationship here. Like cherry blossoms and concrete."

He chuckled, low and dark, and reached for the ashtray, tapping his cigarette.

"But even blossoms gotta pay their dues."

The ash crumbled.

Sakaguchi stood by the door, arms crossed, his gaze a blade against her skin. Nishikado lounged on the couch, idly spinning a lighter between his fingers, grinning like a wolf who’d spotted a lamb. Onizuka, the one-eyed devil, leaned against the filing cabinet, his silence worse than any threat.

Shylock exhaled smoke toward the ceiling. "So. Let’s talk numbers, yeah? You’re what—three months behind? Four?" He didn’t wait for an answer. "See, money's got a funny way of disappearing when you don’t pay it back. And I ain't a charity, sweetheart."

He leaned forward, elbows on the desk, the ink at his collar peeking out like a threat. "But I’m feeling generous today. So here's your choices."

He held up a finger. "One: you pay me everything. Right now."

A second finger. "Two: we work out a new arrangement. You provide… services. Installments, let’s call it."

Third. "Three: well, that's when we repossess ya."
